rows.note: Use 嘥 as the all-purpose colloquial verb for needlessly squandering money, time, or resources.

example.english: I waste money buying useless things.
example.traditional: 我成日嘥錢買啲冇用嘅嘢。
example.jyutping: ngo5 seng4 jat6 saai1 cin2 maai5 di1 mou5 jung6 ge3 je5

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose word for rubbish or discarded material.

example.english: We need to take this bag of waste downstairs to throw away.
example.jyutping: ni1 doi6 laap6 saap3 jiu3 ling1 lok6 gaai1 diu6

rows.note: Use this for wasteful use or consumption, as in a waste of time or money.

example.english: Using water like this is such a waste.
example.jyutping: nei5 gam2 joeng2 jung6 seoi2 hou2 long6 fai3 wo3

rows.note: Use 摧毀 for destroying or devastating something completely, especially in serious or formal contexts.

example.english: War can waste an entire city.
example.traditional: 戰火可以摧毀成個城市。
example.jyutping: zin3 fo2 ho2 ji5 ceoi1 wai2 seng4 go3 sing4 si5

rows.note: Use 用晒 when “waste” means using something up completely.

example.english: The ink is all used up, so don't waste any more.
example.traditional: 啲墨水已經用晒喇，唔好再浪費。
example.jyutping: di1 mak6 seoi2 ji5 ging1 jung6 saai3 laa3 m4 hou2 zoi3 long6 fai3

rows.note: Use 磨蝕 when something is gradually worn away, eroded, or weakened through continual loss.

example.english: Seawater can gradually waste away the rocks by the shore.
example.traditional: 海水慢慢磨蝕岸邊嘅石頭。
example.jyutping: hoi2 seoi2 maan6 maan6 mo4 sik6 ngon6 bin1 ge3 sek6 tau4

rows.note: Use this specifically for excrement and urine, especially when describing animal waste.

example.english: The farm dogs' waste smells awful.
example.jyutping: nung4 coeng4 di1 gau2 si2 niu6 mei6 hou2 cau3
